info.bio:
Cherlyn Sarkisian (nacida en El Centro, California, Estados Unidos, el 20 de mayo de 1946), más conocida como Cher, es una cantante, actriz, compositora, diseñadora y productora estadounidense. Entre sus múltiples premios se encuentran: Óscar, Grammy, Emmy, Globo de Oro y un premio en el Festival de Cine de Cannes.

Denominada como Goddess of Pop (Diosa del Pop), Cher llegó a la fama en 1965, formando parte del dúo musical Sonny & Cher, junto con su ex esposo Sonny Bono. Posteriormente Cher se estableció como solista.

scenes.name: Las cantantes de 1966
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: La primavera de 1966 trajo discos que respiraban apertura, y algunos de los más imaginativos los cantaban mujeres. «Walkin’ My Cat Named Dog» de Norma Tanega (febrero de 1966), producido por Herb Bernstein para Bob Crewe, mezclaba folk y bajo Motown, filosofía y ritmo go-go: una mujer que pasea sola y sin miedo por Nueva York, tan moderna y alusiva como Dylan. Tanega, pintora licenciada y camarera de campamento en los Catskills, se vio de pronto en una gira de seis semanas como única mujer (se cambiaba en un establo) y después en Londres, donde vivió con Dusty Springfield. Nancy Sinatra, con Lee Hazlewood, mezclaba Las Vegas, Los Ángeles, fantasía sadomaso y venganza femenina. Tras los Beatles, el pop británico había quedado dominado por hombres y las cantantes iban juntas en un mismo reportaje: Helen Shapiro no sobrevivió al Merseybeat; Cilla Black (Epstein, versiones de Bacharach/David), Sandie Shaw (una chica Biba descalza, fría y dueña de su imagen, que en «Nothing Comes Easy» canta a una acosadora) y Marianne Faithfull (elegida por su aspecto por Andrew Loog Oldham y arrojada a las giras) eran pioneras por el simple hecho de actuar.

podcast.title: Acting Success (1983, 1988)
podcast.body: Cher was nominated for an Academy Award and won the Golden Globe for Best Supporting Actress in 1983 for her role in "Silkwood." She further cemented her acting career by winning an Academy Award for her role in "Moonstruck" in 1988. "So when Cher was nominated for an Academy Award and won the Golden Globe for Best Supporting Actors in 1983 for Silkwood and won the Academy Award for her role in Moonstruck in 1988, well, I think a lot of people saw the characters in this trilogy of songs as being kind of morphed into a character called Cher."

podcast.title: Career Decline and Resurgence (Late 1970s - 1980s)
podcast.body: Cher's career "fell" in the late 1970s, with her press coverage often focusing on drama with her husband, Greg Allman of the Allman Brothers Band. She later rose again with significant acting success, winning a Golden Globe and an Academy Award. "She fell in the late 70s and if she was in the press at all, it was usually because of the drama with her husband, Greg Almond of the Almond Brothers Band."

podcast.title: Image as "Badass"
podcast.body: Cher was perceived as "badass" with a smoky voice, and her background as not "born privileged" made the narratives of her songs seem plausible to the public. "And her voice was so smoky and she seemed so badass and we were always made aware that Cher was not born privileged, so it all seemed very plausible."

podcast.title: Las Vegas Residency Trend
podcast.body: Cher joined the growing number of pop stars who established Las Vegas residencies, a trend initiated by artists like Celine Dion and Britney Spears. These residencies allowed popular artists to perform to dedicated fan bases in a fixed location, contributing to Las Vegas's evolution as a diverse entertainment destination. "That led to Lady Gaga, Prince, the Backstreet Boys, Mariah Carey, Cher, Shania Twain, Bruno Mars, Adele, and dozens and dozens more."

podcast.title: Not Imperial
podcast.body: Despite her regal status, Cher is arguably not considered an imperial artist because her big hits often have multi-year gaps, and she has frequently missed the top 10 or even the top 40 after scoring a major hit. "As regal as she is, share arguably never has been imperial."

podcast.title: Public Persona in her 40s (Late 1980s - 1990s)
podcast.body: In her 40s, Cher embraced a bold public image, dating much younger men, getting tattoos, and wearing revealing costumes, which was met with approval from many fans who saw it as her embodying her independent spirit. "So when she began dating much younger men and tattooing her body and wearing costumes with her ass hanging out in her 40s and she sold 11 billion copies of Believe in the late 90s, which sure sounds like it would be at home in the 70s to me. A lot of us were saying, damn right she is."

podcast.title: Turned Down "The Night the Lights Went Out in Georgia"
podcast.body: In 1972, songwriter Bobby Russell offered this song to Sonny Bono for Cher to record. However, Sonny turned it down, expressing concern that the song's lyrics, specifically "Don't trust your soul to know backwood's Southern lawyer because the judge in the town's got blood stains on his hands," might offend Cher's Southern fanbase. "Sunny turned the song down because he wasn't sure what shares fans in the South would think about the song."
